newsitem.title: SPAIN: Website disabled by anti-ETA computer users.
newsitem.headline: Website disabled by anti-ETA computer users.

text.p: An Internet site accused of sympathising with ETA guerrillas who killed a Spanish politician has been "mailbombed" out of existence by an avalanche of electronic mail, officials said.

The home page of the Euskal Herria Journal, a New York-based organisation supporting Basque independence, was forced to suspend its operation on Friday after what was described as a "malicious attack" by opponents of the separatist rebels,

The campaign to sabotage the website began after its existence became widely known following the killing last weekend of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, which made international headlines and drew widespread condemnation.

The Institute for Global Communications, a non-profit organisation which describes itself as an Internet services provider for human rights activists, said it was forced to shut down the site because of a "sustained campaign of e-mail mailbombing".

"This destructive campaign has overwhelmed our ability to keep our system running and we have made the difficult decision to suspend the Euskal Herria Journal Web site -- under protest -- so that we can continue to serve the many other individuals and organisations who depend on our services," the group said.
Among the tactics used to overload the website were sending hundreds of duplicate messages, huge files filled with garbled or repetitive messages and large volumes of mail with fake return addresses.

The Institute for Global Communications said the website contained a variety of articles on the Basque separatist movement as well as "hyperlinks" to allow computer users to connect to sites with anti-ETA views.
The Euskal Herria Journal could not be reached for comment.
